title: Financial Literacy and Financial Well-Being of Nurses of a First-Class Province in the Philippines
tldr: A descriptive-correlational study of 178 Filipino public health nurses found high financial literacy (M=3.22) and great financial well-being (M=3.03), with a strong significant correlation between them (r=0.660, p=0.000), though only monthly income predicted literacy level.
problem_and_motivation: Filipino nurses face financial stress due to low wages (average ₱14,492/month for private nurses), COVID-19 salary cuts, and heavy workloads. Only 33% of adults worldwide are financially literate (S&P/GFLEC, 2022). The study aimed to assess the financial literacy and well-being of public health nurses and determine demographic associations, providing baseline data for a Financial Literacy Program.
approach: Descriptive-correlational design with 178 randomly stratified permanent public health nurses in a first-class Philippine province. A researcher-made 52-item questionnaire (4-point Likert scale) assessed financial literacy (knowledge + behavior) and financial well-being (discipline, security, resilience). Validity: Lawshe's CVR=0.91. Reliability: Cronbach's alpha 0.904-0.945. Statistical analysis: frequency, percentage, mean, SD, Pearson correlation, Point Biserial, Rank Biserial, Spearman Rank Correlation.
findings: Overall financial literacy was 'High' (M=3.22; SD=0.39). Overall financial well-being was 'Great' (M=3.03; SD=0.46). Only monthly income significantly correlated with financial literacy [r(176)=0.223, p=0.003]. No significant relationship between demographics and financial well-being. Strong correlation between financial literacy and financial well-being [r(176)=0.660, p=0.000]. Higher-income nurses showed very high knowledge and behavior levels. Older nurses with 2+ dependents had very high financial knowledge.

definitions: Financial Literacy: Combination of financial knowledge and behavior crucial for healthy monetary decisions (Xiao & Porto, 2017)
Financial Well-being: State of financial discipline, financial security, and financial resilience (CFPB, 2018)
Personal Financial Wellness: Influenced by age, sex, marital status, income, and dependents (Joo, 1998 model)

topic_relevance.mapping_rationale: Core subject of the paper; directly measures financial literacy levels using knowledge and behavior components
Studies financial behaviors (savings, spending, borrowing, budgeting) as a component of financial literacy

limitations: Small sample size (n=178) restricted to one province
Only nurses as respondents; cannot generalize to other healthcare workers
Limited demographic variables (age, sex, civil status, income, dependents only)
Descriptive-correlational design limits depth of analysis
Cannot claim exact nurses' financial literacy level due to sample constraints
remember_this: Strong correlation (r=0.660) between financial literacy and financial well-being among Filipino nurses. Monthly income is the only significant demographic predictor of literacy level. The study provides baseline data for designing targeted Financial Literacy Programs for healthcare workers in the Philippines.
